I will keep my land in the usual Quzhou pattern: winter wheat followed by summer maize. That is the system I trust most here. I am 70, so I do not want to gamble on crops that need more marketing, more hand labor, or more complicated management. Wheat and maize fit my machinery, fit local water and fertilizer habits, and I know how to manage them without taking too much risk. I will use improved seed, not traditional seed, because I want stable yield and better lodging and disease resistance, but I will avoid overly high input. I will fertilize enough to protect yield, irrigate at the key stages instead of too many times, and keep pesticide use limited to the main disease and insect pressure. For tillage, I will use rotary tillage before wheat because it is straightforward for me, and I will use no-tillage for summer maize after wheat harvest to save time, moisture, and labor in the busy season.
